title: Repeated Array Indexing inside Loop (Unnecessary Address Calculation)
pattern: Accessing the exact same array element multiple times inside a loop using an unchanging index parameter.
why_bad: Forces the CPU/compiler to repeatedly compute memory offsets (pointer arithmetic) and execute array bounds checks, wasting clock cycles on redundant assembly.
detection: Identical array subscripts appearing multiple times within the body of a tight loop.
counterexample: Highly aggressive optimizing compilers successfully inline the pointer arithmetic. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Store the array element in a local temporary variable before the loop or inside the iteration.
